# Settings reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_reference_docs.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every runtime setting, with its default and allowed range. Set them under `knobs:` in
`<runtime-home>/settings/config.yaml`, or override one with an environment variable:
`TESS_CORE_<SECTION>_<NAME>`, for example `TESS_CORE_SUBAGENTS_MAX_LIVE=4`.

See [Configuration](../configuration.md) for how the files fit together.


## `agent`

| Setting | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent.artifact_acquisition_failure_limit` | `3` | 1..100 | Artifact-read failures tolerated before the progress guard intervenes. |
| `agent.hook_timeout_ms` | `60000` | 500..3600000 | Default milliseconds a hook command may run; per-hook timeouts win. |
| `agent.max_question_nudges` | `3` | 0..20 | Maximum [REPLY REQUIRED] nudges before an unanswered child question is backstopped. |
| `agent.no_progress_limit` | `12` | 2..1000 | Consecutive no-progress turns tolerated before the turn is stopped. |
| `agent.repeated_tool_cycle_limit` | `3` | 2..100 | Identical tool-call cycles tolerated before the progress guard intervenes. |

## `comms`

| Setting | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `comms.inline_result_bytes` | `48000` | 4096..512000 | Inline byte allowance for inter-agent payloads (SendMessage/Agent tool results and drained child messages) before artifact spill or truncation; they are conversation, not raw command output. |
| `comms.reply_poll_ms` | `500` | 50..10000 | Milliseconds between reply-mailbox polls while a SendMessage call is blocked waiting for a reply. |
| `comms.reply_timeout_ms` | `300000` | 1000..3600000 | Default milliseconds a SendMessage(expects_reply=true) call waits for the counterpart's reply before returning a visible non-answer. |

## `daemon`

| Setting | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `daemon.auth_timeout_ms` | `2000` | 25..30000 | Milliseconds a connecting client gets to complete the daemon auth handshake. |
| `daemon.boot_grace_ms` | `300000` | 1000..3600000 | Milliseconds a booting daemon's not-yet-running state file is honored before the boot is treated as wedged and the instance replaced. |
| `daemon.close_grace_ms` | `250` | 25..30000 | Milliseconds the daemon transport waits for a client connection to close cleanly during shutdown. |
| `daemon.dead_work_grace_ms` | `900000` | 1000..86400000 | Milliseconds a task record whose process has died keeps its last status before the boot sweep finalizes it as lost. |
| `daemon.dispatch_drain_ms` | `5000` | 100..300000 | Milliseconds in-flight daemon RPC dispatches get to finish before shutdown cancels them. |
| `daemon.events_rotate_bytes` | `33554432` | 65536..1073741824 | Byte size at which a daemon instance's events log is rotated. |
| `daemon.events_rotate_check_ms` | `300000` | 1000..3600000 | Milliseconds between the daemon's checks of its events log for size-based rotation. |
| `daemon.events_tail_bytes` | `65536` | 4096..16777216 | Bytes read from the tail of a daemon events log when loading recent events. |
| `daemon.health_tick_ms` | `2000` | 100..300000 | Milliseconds between the task supervisor's health reconcile sweeps. |
| `daemon.heartbeat_ms` | `3000` | 50..60000 | Milliseconds between the runtime's liveness checks of its containment daemon; a dead daemon is replaced by exactly one fresh instance. |
| `daemon.instance_lock_timeout_ms` | `5000` | 100..30000 | Milliseconds to wait for the per-instance daemon-ensure lock before giving up on daemon startup coordination. |
| `daemon.instance_reap_ms` | `3600000` | 60000..86400000 | Milliseconds a dead daemon instance's on-disk directory is kept for diagnosis before the garbage collector removes it. |
| `daemon.live_work_cache_ttl_ms` | `30000` | 0..600000 | Milliseconds the supervisor's live-work verdict cache stays fresh before process liveness is re-verified. |
| `daemon.mailbox_watch_ms` | `1500` | 100..60000 | Milliseconds between the containment daemon's sweeps of live children's mailboxes for unannounced to_parent messages (the parent-wake signal). |
| `daemon.owner_poll_ms` | `2000` | 50..60000 | Milliseconds between the containment daemon's liveness checks of its owner runtime process; owner death kills all owned workers and exits the daemon. |
| `daemon.rpc_timeout_ms` | `30000` | 25..300000 | Default milliseconds a daemon RPC may run before the client fails the call; explicit per-call overrides win. |
| `daemon.start_timeout_ms` | `30000` | 25..600000 | Milliseconds to wait for a starting containment daemon to accept connections before startup is failed. |

## `scheduler`

| Setting | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scheduler.clock_check_ms` | `30000` | 1000..3600000 | Longest the scheduler's timer sleeps before re-reading the wall clock and the job records: a machine that slept, a changed clock or a job written by another process is noticed within this. It sleeps less when a job is due sooner and wakes at once for jobs added through this process. |
| `scheduler.max_late_ms` | unset | 1000.. | How late a scheduled job may still fire after its time (the host was down or asleep); a later fire is skipped with a visible notice. Unset: no bound; it fires late and says by how much. |

## `sessions`

| Setting | Default | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessions.background_max_provider_calls` | unset | 1.. | Provider calls a background turn the runtime starts itself (continuity for a child's message) may make before it is ended. Unset: no ceiling. |
| `sessions.background_max_tool_calls` | unset | 1.. | Tool calls a background turn the runtime starts itself may make before it is ended. Unset: no ceiling. |
| `sessions.background_max_wait_ms` | `120000` | 100..3600000 | Milliseconds the oldest waiting background turn of a session (a child's message, a monitor delivery) may wait behind user turns before it takes the next slot. The age is never reset by newer arrivals. |
| `sessions.background_timeout_ms` | unset | 1.. | Milliseconds a background turn the runtime starts itself may run before it is ended. Unset: no ceiling. |
| `sessions.idle_close_ms` | `900000` | 50..86400000 | Milliseconds an open session may stay idle (no turn running, nothing queued) before the runtime unloads it. It stays resumable and any turn reopens it; having children is not a reason to stay open. |
| `sessions.monitor_claim_lease_ms` | unset | 1000..300000 | Lease taken on a monitor delivery while the runtime works on it, renewed while the work runs; a crashed runtime's claim expires after it. Unset: the controller's maximum, 300000 (a lease is fencing, not a ceiling). |
| `sessions.monitor_cleanup_ms` | unset | 1.. | Milliseconds reserved at the end of the delivery deadline for failure bookkeeping and cancellation cleanup (at most a third of it). Unset: no reserve; cleanup is cancel-and-quarantine. |
| `sessions.monitor_poll_ms` | `1000` | 100..3600000 | Milliseconds between the runtime's monitor intake polls: observe every monitor, then offer pending deliveries to their sessions. |
| `sessions.monitor_renew_ms` | `500` | 50..60000 | Milliseconds between lease renewals while a monitor delivery is worked on; a renewal is also where a stop or mute is noticed and the work abandoned. |
| `sessions.monitor_total_deadline_ms` | unset | 1.. | Milliseconds one monitor delivery (claim, authoring, checkpoint, publication) may take in total. Unset: no ceiling. |
| `sessions.pending_retry_ms` | unset | 1.. | Base delay before pending work for a session the host answered Unavailable(retry=True) is offered again; it doubles per refusal up to 15 minutes. Unset: offered again at the daemon's next announcement. |
